newsitem.title: UK: Gdansk refinery says Q2 gasoline needs covered.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk refinery says Q2 gasoline needs covered.

text.p: Poland's second largest refinery Gdansk will not need to buy spot gasoline during a scheduled turnaround that started on Monday, a trader at the refinery said on Tuesday.
Term contracts totalling 140,000 tonnes of Eurograde and regular unleaded gasoline have already covered requirements at the 60,000 barrel per day plant, the trader said.

"It is not necessary to be in the spot market in the next couple of months because we are covered with term contracts," the trader said. "Unless some extra quantities are needed I don't expect to be in the spot market."

He said the turnaround will end June 20 and will include both maintenance and upgrading. The 140,000 tonnes purchased are roughly equal to the refinery's gasoline output over the seven weeks, or about 2,857 tonnes per day, he said.
"We purely rely on imports of gasoline as far as our domestic sales are concerned," he added.
The head of the refinery said earlier this year that it would import a total of 500,000 tonnes of refined oil products to maintain its sales during the turnaround.
